paragraphs.en: Two to eight players take turns filling a score sheet. Each turn fills one cell, from left to right within the chosen row. When all sheets are full, add scores and bonuses; the highest total wins.
Roll all five dice first. You can reroll selected dice up to twice, or record a result immediately. After the third roll, you may also cross out an open cell. A cross scores nothing.

A pair, two pairs of different values, three or four of a kind count only the matching dice. Straights count four or five consecutive values. A full house is three dice of one value and two of another. Five of a kind, full house and Chance count all five dice.
School has one row for each face. Three matching dice qualify. Each die above three goes into that face's reserve. Two sixes and one reserve six qualify later, but score only twelve.

The first player to complete a row without a cross gets its last score again. The first to complete a column without crosses gets 60 points for that column. A school cross removes bonuses you already earned.

One or two columns disable bonuses. Optional even and odd rows require every die to have the chosen parity. Fixed scoring replaces points for triple, small straight, large straight, full house, four of a kind and five of a kind with 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 and 50. First-roll doubling never applies to school. Strict school crosses also block future bonuses.

Enter rolls the dice. Use 1 to 6 to select a die showing that face, and Shift with the same digit to keep it instead. Space reads the dice. With no dice selected, Enter opens scoring after a roll. V opens your sheet, Shift+V another player's sheet, and S reads the totals.
